High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Gwalior
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The petitioner has filed this writ petition challenging the order dated 26/2/2024 (Annexure P/1),
whereby, respondent no.6 has directed not to take any official work from the petitioner.

He has also challenged the order dated 28/2/2024 (Annexure P/2), whereby, the Chief Block Medical Officer,
Community Health Centre, Karera has directed the Medical Officer of Primary Health Centre,
Sirsaud (Karera) not to take any official work from the petitioner.

The petitioner has further challenged the order dated 26/2/2024 (Annexure P/10), whereby, a direction has been issued by respondent no.6 to register an FIR against the petitioner.
2. At the outset, it be noted that in furtherance of order dated 26/2/2024 (Annexure P/10), an FIR has already been registered against the petitioner and as per the submission of petitioner, the same has been challenged by him in a separate writ petition W.P. No.30183/2025, wherein, this Court has already issued notices to respondents and granted interim relief to the petitioner.

Thus, challenge to order dated 26/2/2024 (Annexure P/10) is, therefore, not being considered in NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:20881 2 WP-13536-2024 the instant writ petition and the petitioner is at liberty to pursue the relief in this regard in W.P. No.30183/2025.
3. The facts necessary for decision of this case are that the petitioner belongs to Manjhi Community.
He was appointed as Pharmacists Grade II as a Schedule Caste Category candidate.
The appointment was initially on probation for a period of two years and upon successful completion of probation, the petitioner was confirmed in service vide order dated 28/3/2019.
He has also been conferred benefit of increment on account of his confirmation in service vide order dated 28/3/2019.

sentences.text: The respondent no.9, who claims to be an RTI Activist, made a complaint against the petitioner with regard to his caste certificate.

Taking cognizance of the complaint, respondent no.6 sought verification of the petitioner's caste certificate from Sub-Divisional Officer (Revenue), Lashkar,
Gwalior vide memo dated 20/12/2023 (Annexure R/2).
In response, the Sub- Divisional Officer informed that the certificate in question has not been found issued from his office vide memo dated 17/1/2024 (Annexure R/3).

5. Acting upon the information supplied by Sub-Divisional Officer, the impugned order dated 26/2/2024 (Annexure P/1) was passed by respondent no.6, whereby, on account of petitioner's caste certificate having been found forged and fabricated, he directed the Chief Block Medical Officer, Primary Health Centre, Karera, District Shivpuri, not to take any official work from the petitioner.
Consequent order thereof was passed by the Chief Block Medical Officer, directing the Medical Officer of Primary Health Centre, Sirsaud not to take any official work from the petitioner.

These two orders viz. order dated 26/2/2024 (Annexure P/1) and order dated 28/2/2024 (Annexure P/2) have been challenged NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:20881 3 WP-13536-2024 by the petitioner in the instant writ petition.
6. The learned counsel for the petitioner, challenging the impugned orders, submitted that the directions issued by respondent no.6 are ex-facie illegal and without any jurisdiction.

It is his submission that respondents ought to have adopted the procedure as prescribed under M.P. Civil Services (Classification, Control & Appeal) Rules, 1966 (for short "CCA Rules") and the impugned action of the respondents is not supported with any statutory provisions.

entities.text: M.P. Civil Services (Classification, Control & Appeal) Rules, 1966
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It is his submission that as per the instructions issued by the State Government, the jurisdiction to verify social status of an incumbent lies with the High Power Caste Scrutiny Committee and the respondents cannot enquire into the same at the departmental level.

In support of his submission, he placed reliance upon the Apex Court decision rendered in the case of Kumari Madhuri Patil & Anr. vs. Additional Commissioner & Ors. reported in AIR 1995 SC 94 , particularly para 12 & 13 thereof.

entities.text: Kumari Madhuri Patil & Anr. vs. Additional Commissioner & Ors. reported in AIR 1995 SC 94
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned counsel also submitted that in compliance of impugned order dated 26/2/2024, no work is being taken from the petitioner and consequently, he has not been paid salary since March' 2024.
The illegal action on the part of the respondents is causing not only mental but also financial hardships to the petitioner and his family.
He therefore, prayed for setting aside of the impugned orders.

7. On the other hand, counsel for the State supported the impugned action of the respondents and submitted that on verification, the petitioner's caste certificate has been found to be forged and fabricated, and therefore, his very appointment on the post of Pharmacist Grade II is illegal.
He further submitted that the impugned orders have been passed in exercise of statutory and administrative duties based upon credible complaint and the preliminary enquiry report.

It is his submission that the Apex Court judgment in the case of Madhuri Patil (supra) is NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:20881 4 WP-13536-2024 not applicable in the facts of the present case inasmuch as the dispute as to whether an incumbent belongs to a particular caste or not can only be referred to High Power Committee.
He submitted that the dispute in the present case is about the genuineness of petitioner's caste certificate which can be enquired into by the employer.
He further submitted that the impugned action taken against the petitioner is not punitive but is only administrative in nature.

The learned counsel also submitted that in the similar Mahendra Singh Batham vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190583399/
2 circumstances, an FIR has been registered by STF for offence under Sections 120-B, 420, 468 & 471 of IPC against the persons on account of their securing job based upon forged and fabricated caste certificate.

In support of his submission, learned counsel for the State placed reliance upon the judgment rendered by the Coordinate Bench of this Court in the case of Bharat Singh Batham Vs.
Life Insurance Corporation of India & Ors. in W.P. No.14571/2020 which has been affirmed by the Division Bench in W.A. No.390/2021.

entities.text:
Bharat Singh Batham Vs.
Life Insurance Corporation of India & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He thus, prayed for dismissal of the writ petition.

8. Considered the arguments and perused the record.
9.

So far as the present writ petition is concerned, this Court is required to examine the validity of the impugned orders dated 26/2/2024 (Annexure P/1) and 28/2/2024 (Annexure P/2) only passed by respondents no.6 & 8 respectively.

By the aforesaid two orders, the authorities have directed not to take any official work from the petitioner on account of the fact that his caste certificate has been found to be forged and fabricated.
10. Admittedly, there is no enquiry conducted by the respondents so far.

The impugned action has been taken based upon the information supplied by the Sub-Divisional Officer (Revenue), Lashkar,
Gwalior, wherein, he has only stated that the petitioner's caste certificate dated 19/10/2002 has not been found registered in his Office.

Thus, the petitioner is made to sit at home without NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:20881 5 WP-13536-2024 payment of salary since February'
2024 without conducting any enquiry and affording opportunity to the petitioner.
11. The learned counsel for the petitioner is correct in submitting that the impugned orders have been passed by respondent no.6 & 8 without any authority.
It is seen that the effect of impugned order is akin to placing an employee under suspension.
However, in the case of suspension, an employee is entitled to payment of subsistence allowance.
In the present case, the petitioner has been kept away from the official work without payment of salary/subsistence allowance.

If the respondent/authorities were of the opinion that on account of the certificate of the petitioner having been found forged and fabricated, the petitioner is required to be kept away from his work, they could have exercised powers under Section 9 of CCA Rules by placing the petitioner under suspension.

In that case, the petitioner was entitled to payment of subsistence allowance However,
without doing so, the petitioner has been kept away from his official work and is thus deprived of even the subsistence allowance which he was entitled even in case of suspension.
12. The impugned orders passed by the respondents are thus found to have been passed by respondent no.6 & 8 without even examining the relevant provisions of CCA Rules.
The petitioner has been put to serious financial hardships for last one year on account of aforesaid arbitrary action on the part of respondents.
Accordingly, the order dated 28/2/2024 (Annexure P/1) and order dated 28/2/2024 (Annexure P/2) are set aside.
The respondents are directed to take back the petitioner in service.

Since, this Court has found the action of the respondent no.6 & 8 to be fully without jurisdiction, the petitioner shall be entitled to payment of salary for the period from March' 2024 till date, if not already paid NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:20881 6 WP-13536-2024 to him.

14. With the aforesaid, the writ petition is allowed and disposed of.
